choices.text: Zero, because the velocity is constant
Equal to the gradient of the s-t graph

questions.feedback: If you read the straight line as speeding up, that is the trap: A straight s-t graph means constant acceleration. Reteach point: The gradient of s-t is velocity: a straight s-t graph has constant velocity and zero acceleration.
questions.misconception: A straight s-t graph means constant acceleration.
questions.prompt: An s-t graph is a straight line. What is the acceleration of the motion?

questions.answer: The velocity is the gradient of the s-t graph: the change in displacement divided by the change in time between two points on the line.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the gradient of the s-t graph and rise over run. An answer that reads off a single displacement value with no division by time is incomplete.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain how to find the velocity from an s-t graph.

questions.feedback: Gradient = (40 - 10)/(6 - 0) = 5, so the velocity is 5 m/s. If you answered 30 m/s, you found the rise but forgot to divide by the run.
questions.prompt: An s-t graph passes through (0, 10) and (6, 40). What is the velocity?

questions.answer: The area under a v-t graph is the displacement; here it is 5 x 6 = 30 m.
questions.feedback: The area under the v-t graph is the displacement. For the flat line the area is a rectangle, 5 m/s times 6 s, giving 30 m.
questions.prompt: State what the area under a v-t graph represents, and what it equals for a flat v-t line at 5 m/s lasting 6 s.
